about: Recurring cast of the stick story Shorts. The look is drawn by shorts/design_kit/stick-kit.jsx (Stick component, who=<id>) — never redraw a character by hand in art.jsx. Each video works on its own, but characters keep their history (add a line to 'history' after each episode).
style: Hand-drawn white stick figures on near-black, black-filled round heads, one signature colour accent per character; brand yellow (#F5D33A) for the key caption word. Handwritten captions (Caveat Brush).

arjun.name: Arjun
arjun.look: messy spiky hair (4 strands), yellow scarf (#F5D33A)
arjun.personality: kind, funny, smart — and an overthinker. Reads into every silence.
arjun.speech: short, anxious inner monologue: 'He's mad at me.' 'I definitely did something.'

relationships.maya: close friend who calls him out

history: ep 1 (arjun-mind-reading): mind reading — thinks Kabir is mad; Kabir just had headphones on
ep 2 (arjun-borrow-notes): Ben Franklin effect — does Zoe favors, nothing; on Maya's advice borrows Zoe's notes; now borrows too many pens

maya.name: Maya
maya.look: high ponytail with a coral tie (#FF6B5B)
maya.personality: blunt, confident, funny; says the thing everyone is thinking.
history: ep 1 (maya-bat-and-ball): bat-and-ball — answers 10 cents instantly; Arjun checks; still says the question was rigged
ep 2 (maya-big-ask): door-in-the-face — asks Kabir to help move all weekend, he says no, then carries the couch; Maya has a bookshelf next

kabir.name: Kabir
kabir.look: flat hair, teal headphones (#3FC1C9) always on
kabir.personality: easygoing, cheerful, completely oblivious to drama he 'causes'.
history: ep 1 (kabir-two-days): planning fallacy — essay "two days, tops", all-nighter with Arjun
ep 2 (kabir-tetris-dreams): Tetris effect — block game all weekend, sees falling blocks in bed, stacks Arjun's books; opens the game instead of studying
ep 3 (kabir-late-samaritan): Good Samaritan / hurry — late for an exam, runs past a slumped man; next time stops, still late

zoe.name: Zoe
zoe.look: lavender beanie (#B79CFF) and round lavender glasses
zoe.personality: thoughtful, polite, a people-pleaser who can't say no.
zoe.speech: soft and over-apologetic: 'Sorry, it's totally fine!'
history: ep 1 (zoe-tiny-favor): foot-in-the-door — holds Maya's coffee, ends up covering her weekend shift
ep 2 (zoe-repeat-order): mirroring — café job, tiny tips (Maya tips one coin); repeats orders word for word, Maya calls her a parrot

episode_rules: Structure: pattern interrupt in the first line (something happens) -> problem -> escalation (viewer predicts) -> 'But…' reveal of what was really going on -> name the psychology effect plainly -> payoff that reframes the opening; optionally a small unresolved character beat at the end.
20–40 s. 1–3 cast members per episode. Psychology stays accurate: any study or number must be verified; for real experiments say 'Arjun isn't real, but this experiment was.'
Each line can carry 'label' (1–2 grey corner words) and 'tone' (ElevenLabs tags).
